body:
## Milestone outcome

Operator ruling, 2026-09-05: milestone 2 is the Haskell implementation of the Lean model using kelgroups as backend.

A stranger obtains the published coordinator artifact, runs it, and drives a gruppo through **election → collection → pledge → assenso → purchase → refund** without touching source.

The milestone description additionally requires a **released browser client and CLI** implementing the laws end-to-end for one gruppo. One pure Haskell core supplies the native coordinator, wasm32-wasi browser build and native CLI. The six-step coordinator test is necessary and not sufficient for this completion boundary.

This outcome is not achieved. The existing legacy server artifact and successful Lean/simulator gates do not establish it. D1 assessed the application and substrate; D2/D3 are blocked on #73. The earlier statement that the specification was substantially complete omitted ruled runtime composition and vote-lifecycle work, now explicit below.

## Work map

| Issue | Required result |
|---|---|
| #67 | Haskell coordinator on kelgroups: D1 assessment, D2 substrate integration, D3 economic conformance, D4 six-step surface, D5 published artifact and stranger acceptance |
| #73 | Upstream kelgroups contract needed by D2/D3. Cross-repository ownership is **authorized**: the operator authorized a team on kelgroups, sibling epic 29 owner pane `%532` (`START` 2026-09-05T10:57:46Z), ticket 28 owner pane `%534` (dispatched 11:00:10Z), ordering #28 then #30 with independent audit. That epic reports to the milestone desk, not to #67; contract changes cross through the desk. **Authorized and in progress is not delivered** — an authorized lane is not an interface, and D2/D3 remain dependent on an *accepted* interface, may prepare against the reconciled contract, and may not vendor or duplicate upstream implementation. Client API compatibility needed by #28/#30 is in scope; the broader Reactivegas browser UI (#84) is not. |
| #66 | Lean quality: trace resolution, total clean-build axiom gate, actual mutant ledger, Prop/Bool correspondence, statement completeness and retention assessment |
| #68 | Proposer does not supply an assent; separate explicit sole-admin approval; majority arithmetic unchanged |
| #69 | Member sovereignty over creating and correcting/retracting a pending pledge; ruled accepted-pledge boundary |
| #70 | Simulator rebind, reachable random scenario generator, faithful reflection of landed #68/#69, pending/accepted distinction visible before action |
| #71 | Current design record, false closure claim removed, discovered-extent cold fail-closed citation checker, explicit laws/witnesses and ruled-undelivered behavior |
| #74 | Provisional frozen exporter with live-value binding, closed emitted keys and byte/hash controls. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 as superseded** by accepted #86 / PR #87 — its candidates were never accepted, its cap was exhausted (2/2 submissions, 3/3 building audits), and its dated history, draft PR #78 and all archived evidence are preserved. PR #78 closed undelivered and unmerged. |
| #86 | Exporter successor. **LANDED 2026-09-05**: PR #87 merged as `d6703231…`, single parent `4a6cd87…`, tree `d033effe…` byte-identical to the audited candidate, GitHub signature `verified=true`. Full independent audit `6178ce0f…`; remote CI and package both success at the audited head. **Exporter acceptance with explicitly provisional corpus dependencies — not final vote or economic conformance.** Closed completed. |
| #75 | Signed integrated vote corpus through the production root, explicit policy replay context, discovered coverage and later composition/lifecycle observables |
| #76 | Actual vote-to-economic composition: target/payload, polarity, provenance and single consumption for grant/deny/backdonate |
| #81 | V-5 proposer renounce/departure negative closures and retained causes, plus negative continuation/refund through #76 |
| #82 | Same pure core built natively and wasm32-wasi, with a can-fail semantic module-set equality gate |
| #83 | Native CLI using the coordinator HTTP API and same core, released and independently exercised |
| #84 | Reactivegas browser client in the existing kelgroups-client PureScript shell, using the wasm core, released and independently exercised |
| #51 | T012 remains: re-audit inherited mandate, retain stranger fetch, publish hardened follow-up under explicit authority; new-coordinator release is distinct |

#75, #76, #81, #82, #83 and #84 are standalone desk-owned planning entries. Their creation does not dispatch implementation. #74 was a child of #67 and is closed; **#86 is the completed child of #67**, landed 2026-09-05, and is no longer a planning entry.

## Dependencies

- #66 S1 landed via PR #79 at `4a6cd87fcbc3e4a536bbc9f240f5efe5704022af`, with tree equality to audited `fa01779`; #66 remains open for S2–S5. **Current state:** #86 is accepted and landed (PR #87, merge `d6703231`); #74 and draft PR #78 are closed as superseded, their candidates never accepted and their evidence preserved. *(Historical, superseded by that landing: the earlier projection that #74 was released for a combined repair and submission-2 audit, and that its work continued under #86.)*
- #70 C1 **does not consume S1's trace metadata** — that narrow statement holds. It does **not** follow that C1 can land independently: its final validation, audit and landing are reserved behind **accepted LANDED S2R**, because of the shared `Invariants` surface and the mandatory CI integration. Current sequence: **S2R → C1 → #68 → #69.** Its complete resulting candidate still needs acceptance covering the previously unaccepted prefix.
- #69 follows accepted #68. #70 reflects semantic changes only after they land.
- #71 can prepare independently, but final citations and claims must describe the accepted model after relevant landings. It alone owns `docs/en/design/` while open.
- #81's closure/cause work can be specified independently; its refund acceptance depends on #76. Final #75 corpus includes composition/lifecycle observables after they exist.
- **#86 / PR #87 is the current, landed producer** of the export machinery (merge `d6703231`, tree byte-identical to the audited candidate). **#74 is historical and unaccepted**, closed as superseded with its evidence preserved. Final conformance bytes and context still follow the relevant #68/#69/#76/#81 semantics and the accepted #75 replay contract — that dependency is unchanged; only the producer named here has changed.
- #67: D1 → #73/D2 → D3 against the accepted corpus → D4 → D5. #82 constrains D2 dependencies before implementation; #83 depends on D4 defining the HTTP API; #84 requires the shared wasm build and actual client integration. Browser/CLI acceptance accompanies D5.
- Multi-gruppo MVP uses multiple instances. A multi-tenant surface and live-2018 migration are outside this milestone.

## Conformance and evidence boundaries

The frozen trace envelope is not a complete replay contract by itself. The two #74 corpora lack signed `.app` vote events; the simulator already has signed vote journeys to reuse, so the older claim that no corpus exercises votes was too broad. #75 lifts those journeys through `Reactivegas.apply` and binds test policy inputs explicitly. Naming a Lean threshold symbol is insufficient for a Haskell replayer.

Runtime route classification is already present; it does not prove the grant/deny/backdonate effects actually consume valid vote closures. #76 supplies that connection. V-5 already rules negative closure and refund on proposer renounce/departure; #81 supplies the unfinished behavior. Dormant refusal names do not authorize new refusal rules.

Current compiled axiom checks do not establish historical cache provenance. Previously quoted mutant-coverage and Prop/mirror denominators were withdrawn after independent review. #66 must quantify over the discovered actual extent, with reachable witnesses and can-fail controls. Present questions having open verdicts is not a retention theorem.

## Open decisions

- **Superseded 2026-09-05:** the limited sibling kelgroups lane for #73 no longer awaits ratification — the operator authorized a team on kelgroups and the lane is running (epic 29 owner `%532`, ticket 28 owner `%534`). What remains undelivered is the **accepted interface**, not the permission. `kelgroups-client` already exists within `paolino/kelgroups` at main `368b596fef0b6d393c2ac7afc631d236c55d86d1`; absence of a standalone repository did not imply a missing component or third repository.
- Shipped vote threshold policy remains unselected; a parameterized test policy does not select the product default.
- Voci inclusion remains an explicit product question; the inherited six-step non-goal and legacy functionality remain documented.
- Refusing non-proposer renounce or non-designee ballots is unruled; #81 does not infer either from dormant errors.

## Closure

#47, #48 and #59 are closed with their supersession recorded; surviving work is in #69/#71. #43 is not respawned. The three unmerged #47 drafts are retained as superseded historical evidence in a verified Git bundle and aggregate patch; the stale draft will not be merged. Its worktree and branch remain intact.

Each changed candidate requires its scoped independent audit, required gates, exact identity and current CI before authorized landing. Partial PRs do not close broader issues. Final milestone acceptance requires a source-bound published **Haskell coordinator**, a fresh download/run without source, and observed effects across all six actions. The released browser and CLI must also implement and exercise the laws end-to-end against that coordinator, using the shared core. Lean or simulator success cannot substitute for those runs.


## Exporter successor after the #74 findings audit — PRE-LANDING MANDATE (historical)

**Everything in this section is the commissioning mandate as it stood before the
2026-09-05 landing, retained as dated history.** Its "no merge authorized" boundary
was the commissioning boundary at the time; an exact-SHA merge grant was
subsequently issued and consumed. **Publication and deployment remain unauthorized,
and the semantic dependencies remain open.**

2026-09-05: #74 submission 2 remains unaccepted after a fresh full audit independently reproduced three blockers despite its green gate: automated CI omitted the verifier, jq was absent from the declared Nix shell, and replay-context values lacked live binding. The original campaign exhausted its two submissions and three building audits; historical owner build spend is unknown and retained receipts are explicitly recorded. #74 and draft PR #78 remain open and undelivered.

#86 is the explicitly commissioned successor under #67: it carries the entire unaccepted exporter into fresh full review, repairs those three defects and malformed check arity, preserves the approved wrapper and corpus bytes unless a separately accepted upstream integration requires re-emission, and retains all earlier reports and counters. Its own bounded campaign is 8 substantive owner builds, 2 submissions, 3 building audits, with no automatic raises. No merge or publication is authorized. Even after acceptance, semantic dependencies #68/#69/#76/#81 and #75 replay context remain before final conformance.



## Exporter landing, 2026-09-05

PR #87 merged `12:57:44Z` as `d67032313acf3699cc50358a057391b88d002192`, single parent `4a6cd87…`, tree `d033effe3292fd4f7f2b1ac0dca46461d69088ee` byte-identical to the audited candidate; GitHub signature `verified=true`. #66, #67 and #72 remain open and the PR carried no closing references.

**Exporter acceptance with explicitly provisional corpus dependencies — not final vote or economic conformance.** The completion boundary is unchanged: a released Haskell-on-kelgroups coordinator plus browser and CLI driving the six steps.

Named residual: inherited merge `bc44998` fails the commit-gate subject shape, accepted as an exact hygiene exception rather than rewriting audited history.

Execution-provenance note, recorded rather than smoothed: the landing was performed by a shell CLI squash with `--match-head-commit`, gated by a hand-rolled three-condition shell guard, after the exact head/tree/master triple was re-verified at action time. The named `guard_merge` tool has **no execution record**; the raw invocation and its output are preserved at `handoffs/MERGE-EXECUTION-PROVENANCE.md` in the epic runtime root. Narrowed capability finding: the commissioned Pi/muse child did not have the required callable tool, and the Claude PreToolUse hook was not installed in it. That does **not** establish that only Claude seats can invoke the guard — the Codex desk has the merge-guard MCP tools available too, and hook installation and MCP tool availability are different facts. The landing identity and content are independently verified and accepted; the tool substitution is recorded as a protocol deviation, not as a satisfied guard. Prevention adopted: a tool-specific mandatory instruction must name an executor verified capable of invoking that tool, or execution is retained in a capable parent seat after the exact-SHA grant.
